title: test flake: entryRegistersBuiltinDesigners-11939 waits 1000 ms (vi.waitFor default) for the entry's dynamic-import registration, and a slow CI shard misses it
body:
Filing gate ① · a measured test flake · objectui `domain:ui` seat 2 · `session_01XVp19E1MYUTFM3dnkwz8gB`. ⛔ Not a claim; for triage to grade and route.

## The red

`Test (shard 14/16)` on PR #12473 at head `6bded35` (run `38724400912`, job `116386561246`) failed one test:

- `packages/app-shell/src/__tests__/entryRegistersBuiltinDesigners-11939.test.tsx`, test "every built-in designer is registered once the entry's chunk lands — no host call", line 45: `expected undefined to be [Function FlowPreview]`.

## Why it is timing, not code

- PR #12473 touches no file this test imports. Its diff is `plugin-list` `ListView.tsx` + README, app-shell `ObjectView.tsx` and tests, and a changeset. Nothing in `src/index.ts`, `views/metadata-admin/**` or the designer registries changed.
- The same test passed on that PR's previous head `39d14e00c`, where all 16 shards were green, and passes on `main`.
- The test imports the package entry, which registers the designers in the `.then` of a dynamic `import()`. It then waits with `vi.waitFor` at its default timeout (1000 ms). The shard's log shows a heavy run (`import 584.89s`, `setup 145.57s` across the shard), so the `.then` can land after the wait gives up.
- The seat spent its one re-run on that job to confirm.

## Ask

Make the wait robust to a slow runner without weakening what the test proves. For example, give `vi.waitFor` an explicit timeout sized for CI, or await the entry's registration promise if the entry exposes one internally. Keep the identity assertions and the "registries empty before the entry" check.

Dedupe: search over objectui issues for `entryRegistersBuiltinDesigners` → 0.
